text: I am running for the Coronado Unified School District Board because I have the experience and perspective to serve our community well. My husband and I have proudly called Coronado home for 20 years. With our four children now in college, I am excited to give back to the community that has given so much to our family.

For more than 30 years, my work focused on improving the lives of children. I am an attorney, former Juvenile Court judge pro tem, President of Friends of Children United Society (FOCUS), and recently completed my term as Trustee on the Francis Parker School Board, where I also served as Parent Association President. I founded the FOCUS internship program at Coronado High School, mentoring Coronado students.

As a Trustee, I helped implement a campus-wide cell phone ban and later served on CUSD’s task force addressing student cell phone use. I am completing a certificate program on Artificial Intelligence in Education at the University of San Diego to help CUSD thoughtfully address the opportunities and challenges of technology.

As CUSD transitions to Basic Aid, my experience in school governance and financial stewardship will guide sound, long-term decisions. My priorities are student safety and well-being, academic excellence, outstanding teachers, responsible technology policies, and transparent, fiscally responsible governance.

text: Coronado has been my home since 1992. I have a deep, personal investment in the future of our schools. I raised four children here, all of whom attended Coronado Unified schools. Today, I am excited that my granddaughter will soon attend Village Elementary, where her father attended before her.

Education has been the focus of my life’s vocation. I earned a B.S. in Elementary Education from Northern Arizona University and a doctoral degree from Fuller Theological Seminary. My educational pursuits in human development and family education have given me a strong understanding of the importance of preparing students for both academic achievement and life beyond the classroom.
I have served Coronado schools and families as a founding member of the Coronado Middle School PTO, classroom volunteer, and Coronado Recreation coach.

As a School Board member, I will advocate for academic excellence, impactful staff, responsible fiscal stewardship, strong parent engagement, and safe, supportive learning environments. I will listen to our community, work collaboratively, ask thoughtful questions, and make decisions grounded in what is best for students.
I am eager to bring my experience, perspective, and commitment to public service to the Coronado Unified School District.

text: I am running for re-election to continue serving our Coronado community. For the past four years, I oversaw the Bridge to Basic Aid, participated in the Portrait of a Graduate, and championed military families.

I am a mom, attorney, and military spouse. My oldest child graduated from Coronado High School and my other two children attend CHS and . I am deeply-rooted in our schools, volunteering in their classrooms and programs. I value my connections with the administration and teachers and find it is critical when making decision for our district. I help various school groups, boosters, and organizations, maintaining and growing relationships with parents.

As a military spouse, I know the challenges we face and will continue to be a passionate advocate for us. I share our experiences in the board room, Sacramento, and Washington, D.C. to make sure that our voices are heard.
Our Board established a professional and collaborative culture that allows the district to grow our programs while maintaining fiscal responsibility as we champion every child every day.
I look forward to using my experience, knowledge, and relationships on the Board and in the community to lead our district for another four years.
